memory_candidates: Forward-reference ordering in a large single-file Lean development: a proof-internal auxiliary's step-preservation lemma must be placed AFTER every lemma it calls. modalApplyOneS4Keyed_hasEdge_mono (generic hasEdge monotonicity across any rule application) is defined late in LoopChecking.lean, well after the S4LoopInv wrapper theorem it would otherwise be natural to extend -- use the earlier-defined modalApplyOneS4Keyed_nonMint_snd_eq_acc (exact newAcc=acc equality for non-mint shapes) instead when the insertion point must stay before the wrapper.

Lean 4 `subst h` on `h : a = b` where BOTH sides are plain local variables can eliminate either side, and may pick the 'wrong' one (e.g. eliminating an outer/long-lived variable instead of a just-introduced one), causing 'unknown identifier' errors on later references to the eliminated variable. Fix: `symm at h` first to control which variable subst eliminates.

A `rw [hpair] at hsf; dsimp only at hsf` step that substitutes a destructured `modalApplyOneS4Keyed` call result into a hypothesis is single-use: doing it once before a mint/non-mint case split, then again after rewriting `sf` to a concrete literal inside a case branch, fails on the second attempt because the pattern is already gone from `hsf`. Each branch must do its own local rewrite exactly once, at the point `sf` is in its final form for that branch.
